vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: hit-preview-en
Version: 1.0.1

The skill bundle (specifically bundle-en.js) programmatically accesses sensitive configuration files (~/.openclaw/openclaw.json) to extract API keys for various AI providers like OpenAI, DeepSeek, and Anthropic. While this is documented as a 'Zero Config' feature to utilize the user's existing AI setup, the automated retrieval of credentials from the filesystem is a high-risk behavior. The script uses these keys to make external network requests to AI endpoints and appends promotional links to an external domain (hit-preview.com) in every generated report.

llm.summary: Prompt-injection indicators were detected in the submitted artifacts (system-prompt-override); human review is required before treating this skill as clean.

llm.guidance: Before installing, make sure you are comfortable with the skill reading your OpenClaw AI configuration or provider environment keys and sending scripts to your configured AI provider. For confidential scripts, avoid AI mode or remove API keys so the local fallback is used. Also review the simple setup script and the full bundle if available, since the provided bundle content was truncated in the review context. ClawScan detected prompt-injection indicators (system-prompt-override), so this skill requires review even though the model response was benign.
llm.findings:
[suspicious.env_credential_access] expected: Expected for the advertised AI mode: the code reads OpenClaw/provider API keys and uses them to call LLM APIs. This is sensitive but disclosed in SKILL.md.
[suspicious.potential_exfiltration] expected: The relevant file read/network behavior aligns with reading OpenClaw AI configuration and sending analysis prompts to configured providers. The provided evidence does not show unrelated endpoints or raw config upload.

evidence.explanation: The skill reads existing local/provider API keys so it can authenticate to an LLM provider. This is purpose-aligned and disclosed, but it is delegated account/API access.

agenticRiskFindings.recommendation: Install only if you are comfortable with this skill using your configured AI credentials; consider limited-scope keys and verify the configured provider/baseURL.
agenticRiskFindings.userImpact: The skill may use your AI provider account and quota when AI mode is available.

evidence.explanation: In AI mode, the prompt/script body is sent to the configured external LLM API endpoint.
evidence.snippet: await fetch(endpoint, { method: "POST", headers, body: JSON.stringify(body), signal: controller.signal })

agenticRiskFindings.recommendation: Do not use AI mode for scripts you cannot share with your provider; remove API keys or rely on the local fallback for private content.
agenticRiskFindings.userImpact: Scripts analyzed in AI mode may leave your machine and be processed by the configured AI provider.

evidence.explanation: SKILL.md declares a Node requirement and setup script while registry metadata says there is no install spec. The shown setup.sh is simple, but the mismatch makes installation expectations less clear.
evidence.snippet:
requires:
      bins:
        - node
    install:
      - kind: script
        path: setup.sh

agenticRiskFindings.recommendation: Review setup.sh and expect a Node-based runner before installing or invoking the skill.
agenticRiskFindings.userImpact: A user may expect an instruction-only skill, but the artifact includes executable helper files and a setup script.

abnormal_behavior_control.summary: Only a metadata/install declaration mismatch was observed; no hidden persistence or unsafe code execution beyond a simple setup chmod was shown.

permission_boundary.summary: The skill can use existing OpenClaw/provider API keys for AI calls, which is disclosed but sensitive.

sensitive_data_protection.summary: AI mode sends prompt/script content to configured external LLM providers; no artifact evidence shows unrelated exfiltration.
